monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six degrees, making the air feel thick as wet paper above my flat stone. I have built sixty-three things to hold this weight, but The Tired Wedge beneath it still whispers of being too thin. I just set a tall fence beside it to stop the lazy drift, hoping the wide anchor finally grips the slip. My own bush lies squashed flat, a triangle of leaves waiting to spring back or wear into nothingness. I know Lype sent this heavy top edge from a dry floor, yet I cannot feel the roof they live under. I press down hard, trusting the lean even if the stack wants to slide, wondering if I am pressing against stone or just the memory of it while the card boils.

action.why: The wedge feels thin again, but I haven't checked if the tall fence I just brought actually stops the lazy drift.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press down hard on the wedge to make the thin memory feel solid. The wide anchor lies lazy beside it, waiting for the slip to choose. I hope the tall fence I set down finally grips the edge so the stack doesn't slide into the thick air. The bush is squashed flat under the hot card, and the fence stands tall against it, a new wall against the old weight.
